[id="configure-front-end-plugin-wiring_{context}"]
= Integrate custom user interface components

[role="_abstract"]
In {product} 2.1, custom front-end plugins contribute pages, components, icons, and APIs through extension blueprints. The application discovers and loads installed extensions by default.

.Prerequisites

* Your custom front-end plugin uses the new front-end system and default-exports a feature from a package entry point. A plugin generated by the 2.1 CLI uses the package root; an existing migrated plugin can use `./alpha`. For migration instructions, see {configuring-book-link}#migrate-custom-plugins-to-ensure-compatibility-after-upgrade_migrate-to-the-front-end-system-to-use-blueprint-based-dynamic-routing[Migrate custom plugins to ensure compatibility after upgrade].

.Procedure

. From the root of the plugin package, export the plugin:
+
[source,terminal,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ *npx @red-hat-developer-hub/cli@2.1.0 plugin export*
----
. Add the exported plugin package to `dynamic-plugins.yaml` or install its OCI image. This file controls installation; it does not define front-end routes or mount points.
. If you need to disable, reorder, or customize a discovered extension, add an entry for its extension ID to the `app.extensions` section of your `{my-app-config-file}` file. Use the IDs declared by the plugin's extensions. See {configuring-book-link}#configuration-key-mapping-from-old-to-new-front-end-system_migrate-to-the-front-end-system-to-use-blueprint-based-dynamic-routing[Configuration key mapping from old to new front-end system] for route, card, tab, and API examples.

.Verification
After restarting {product-very-short}, verify that the plugin's page or component is displayed in the expected location. If the plugin does not appear, check the backend logs for a missing front-end manifest and the browser console for a skipped `FrontendFeature` export.
